title: Dismissed Laguna mayor faces graft, unlawful appointment cases
summary: The Ombudsman has ordered criminal charges filed against dismissed Luisiana, Laguna Mayor Jomapher Uy Alvarez over two separate cases.

blocks.text: November 16, 2026 | 5:11pm
Dismissed Luisiana, Laguna Mayor Jomapher Uy Alvarez as seen in a photo posted in 2022.
Alvarez via FB

MANILA, Philippines — The Office of the Ombudsman has ordered criminal charges filed against dismissed Luisiana, Laguna Mayor Jomapher Uy Alvarez over the withholding of benefits from former municipal officials and the appointment of an unqualified municipal administrator.
In a statement Monday, November 16, the Ombudsman said it found grounds to charge Alvarez with graft and unlawful appointment under Article 244 of the Revised Penal Code.

The Ombudsman also found Alvarez administratively liable for grave misconduct and violating Section 5 of Republic Act 10154, imposing a dismissal penalty even though he had already been removed from office in an earlier case.
Withheld benefits. The graft case stemmed from a complaint filed by former municipal officials Nestor Alcala Rondilla and Ness Rondilla, whose three-year terms ended on June 30, 2022.
The complainants accused Alvarez of refusing to release their year-end bonuses and cash gifts despite their entitlement to the benefits.
Alvarez denied the allegations, claiming the complaint was politically motivated and that he had never received the letters requesting the release of the funds.
The Ombudsman rejected his defense as self-serving and unsupported by evidence.
It found Alvarez administratively liable for grave misconduct and violating Section 5 of RA 10154, which governs the timely release of retirement benefits.

Although Alvarez had already been dismissed from service following an earlier complaint filed by Rondilla, the Ombudsman imposed another dismissal penalty and ordered the continued enforcement of its accessory penalties.
Unlawful appointment

In a separate case, the Ombudsman ordered Alvarez charged under Article 244 of the Revised Penal Code for appointing Emmanuel Babaan Villamin as municipal administrator in 2022 despite his failure to meet the position's qualifications.

According to the Ombudsman, the municipal government advertised the position with requirements including a college degree, first-grade Civil Service Commission (CSC) eligibility and at least three years of management and administrative experience.
Less than a month later, Alvarez signed Villamin's appointment despite his failure to meet the requirements.
The CSC formally disapproved the appointment in March 2023, prompting Villamin to step down.

Alvarez and municipal human resource management officer I Liza Ludovice Oblenida argued that their roles in the appointment process were merely recommendatory, as the CSC had final authority to approve or reject appointments.
The Ombudsman rejected their defense, stressing that the mayor's appointing authority under the Local Government Code carries a legal responsibility to ensure compliance with civil service rules.

"Respondent Alvarez cannot feign ignorance of the lack of qualifications of respondent Villamin because aside from knowing the latter personally, the basic requirements for the position are spelled out in the job portal, as embodied in Section 480 of the LGC, which respondent Alvarez ought to know," the Ombudsman's decision read.
In the administrative aspect of the appointment case, the Ombudsman imposed a separate suspension of one month and one day without pay on Alvarez.
Oblenida was also given the same suspension after being found administratively liable for simple neglect of duty.

The Ombudsman said the suspensions would be converted into fines equivalent to the respondents' salaries for the same period if they could no longer be enforced because of separation from government service.
